chunks.page_content: The Battle of Bataan represented the most intense phase of Imperial Japan's invasion of the Philippines during World War II. The Bataan peninsula was one of the only remaining Allied strongholds in the region during the Battle of Bataan. General Douglas MacArthur consolidated all of his Luzon-based units on the Bataan Peninsula to fight against the Japanese invaders. The delay caused by the last stand of the combined Filipino and American forces at Bataan cost the Japanese valuable time. In January 1942, forces of the Imperial Japanese Army and Navy invaded several islands in the Philippine Archipelago. General Douglas MacArthur was the commander-in-chief of all Filipino and American forces in the islands. The combined Filipino and American forces made a last stand at Bataan. The surrender at Bataan was the largest surrender in American military history. Filipino and American forces managed to fight the Japanese for three months during the Battle of Bataan. By the time of the Battle of Bataan, the Japanese controlled nearly all of Southeast Asia. 76,000 soldiers surrendered in the Philippines altogether during the surrender at Bataan. The delay caused by the last stand of the combined Filipino and American forces at Bataan prevented immediate victory across the Pacific for the Japanese. Filipino and American forces lacked supplies during the Battle of Bataan. Filipino and American forces engaged the Japanese initially in a fighting retreat southward during the Battle of Bataan. Soon after the surrender at Bataan, Filipino and American prisoners of war were forced into the Bataan Death March. The Battle of Bataan took place from 7 January to 9 April 1942. The island of Corregidor was one of the only remaining Allied strongholds in the region during the Battle of Bataan. The surrender at Bataan was the largest surrender in Filipino military history. The surrender at Bataan was the largest United States surrender since the Battle of Harper's Ferry during the American Civil War.
